prompt:
A LANDSCAPE FRAME, exactly 4:3 (four wide by three tall). NOT portrait, NOT square.

An ancient stone prayer wall seen straight on from a few steps away, filling the whole frame edge to edge: great weathered blocks of warm honey-and-cream limestone, worn smooth, with deep dark seams and cracks running between the courses where folded paper notes could be tucked. The lowest course meets a strip of packed sandy ground along the very bottom edge. Dusk light — the sky is not visible; the wall fills the frame — with warm golden lamplight falling from the upper left and soft violet-blue shadow gathering at the right and along the bottom.

THE WALL MUST BE COMPLETELY BARE. No paper, no notes, no folded slips, no scraps, no candles, no lanterns, no flames, no flowers, no plants, no ivy, no moss, no people, no hands, no animals, no text, no lettering, no numbers, no carvings, no inscriptions, no symbols, no cross, no star, no graffiti, no objects of any kind on the wall or on the ground in front of it. Nothing whatsoever is tucked into the cracks. Notes and candles are drawn on top of this painting, so anything painted onto the wall will be drawn over.

Warm hand-illustrated storybook style with clean flat shapes and soft painted shading — no photorealism, no line art, no watermark, no border, no frame, no vignette. Values kept soft and mid-toned across the stone so small pale objects placed on it stay clearly readable; the cracks are dark and inviting but not black.

REMEMBER: a 4:3 landscape frame, bare weathered stone edge to edge, and NOT ONE THING tucked into it.
